newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - May 2.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- IRELAND HOISTS RATES TO PROTECT THE PUNT

Ireland's central bank yesterday announced a surprise 50-basis point rate rise to defend the punt against a widespread selling campaign. The bank raised the key interest rate, known as the short-term facility rate, to 6.75 percent from 6.25 percent, after a four percent drop in the Irish pound against the Deutschmark.
-- HALIFAX CHANGES STORY ON BONUS QUALIFICATION

The Halifax Building Society yesterday changed its earlier story that qualification rules for windfall shares were based on the Building Societies Act, admitting that many of the 400,000 members who missed out on free shares did so through its own rules. One such rule saw members miss out because their accounts did not reach the 100 stg threshold on qualification date, although interest already earned but not credited would have put them above the cut-off point.
-- SEARS 'DOCTOR' STARTS AT ONCE ON BSC REMEDY

David James has started a programme to either overhaul or break up the British Shoe Corporation, after being called in by Sears Holdings to solve the problems facing the chain. He has told managers to produce a new business plan by May 19, and called in accountants Price Waterhouse to work with the executive.
THE TIMES
-- SFO TO SEEK NADIR ARREST IN TURKEY

The Serious Fraud Office has sent officers to Turkey to try to arrest Asil Nadir and have him brought to Britain if he stands by his stated intention to travel to the mainland from his Northern Cyprus haven. Turkey recently signed the European Union Convention on Extradition that allows extradition for
financial crimes.
-- BAA LEADING RACE FOR MELBOURNE

The British Airports Authority is likely to emerge as winner in the bidding for Melbourne Airport in Australia. The deal is likely to be worth about 630 million stg and represents a key part of BAA's overseas expansion plans. BAA is also bidding for Bali airport in Indonesia with the same partners in its Melbourne consortium.
-- SHELL URGED TO TIGHTEN POLICIES ON ENVIRONMENT

Several of the major shareholders in Shell are considering a vote in favour of a resolution forcing the company to improve its environmental policies. The resolution is being considered by leading insurance companies holding stakes in Shell Transport & Trading. The company has been accused by
environmentalists of operating double standards between its operations in the developed and developing world.
THE GUARDIAN
-- PREDATORS READY TO POUNCE

A new surge in takeover activity is likely in the City over the coming weeks, as corporate financiers resurrect deals put on hold over the election campaign. Analysts predicted at least two big takeover attempts in the near future. Speculation centred on the financial sector, where many suspect B.A.T Industries is about to demerge its financial arm, and then remerge
with another leading insurance firm.
-- FIDELITY BROKERAGE IS FINED 200,000 STG

Fidelity Brokerage, the UK offshoot of the US fund manager, has been fined 200,000 stg plus 162,500 stg costs by the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) for the breakdown of its share-dealing system. The SFA said the fine would have been
bigger, but for the broker's 'significant' loss of revenue,
believed up to 30 million stg.
-- ING SEEKS WALL STREET OUTLET

ING Barings is in talks to buy Wall Street investment bank Dillon Read. ING already owns a 25 percent stake in Dillon Read, inherited when it took over the collapsed Barings, and is understood to be willing to pay over 260 million stg for the rest, more than double its book value, in order to gain a Wall Street footing.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- ELECTION-DAY NERVES DAMPEN TRADING

As Britain went to the polls, fresh evidence emerged of the strength of the economy yesterday. The monthly survey of purchasing managers in industry showed that fears of economic recovery being derailed by the strong pound were unjustified. The April index of activity was up, as were output and export orders. Shares closed at a record high, although trading was quiet and nervous due to caution about the election result.
-- KILLIK JOINS QUEUE TO DISTANCE ITSELF FROM REGAN BID

Stockbroker Killik & Co yesterday moved to distance itself from Andrew Regan's bid for the Co-operative Wholesale Society. A statement from the firm said it regretted the use of dishonest tactics and regretted the association of its name with Regan, as the Stock Exchange launched an inquiry into possible insider
dealing in Lancia Trust.
-- WH SMITH AIMS FOR RECOVERY WITH FEMALE DIRECTOR

British retailer WH Smith Group Plc employed its first female executive director yesterday when it appointed Beverley Hodson as managing director. She replaces Peter Bamford, who left last month as part of the plan to rejuvenate the company's fortunes. She becomes the second woman on the WH Smith board, along with Marjorie Scardino, Pearson chief executive, who is a non-executive director.
